craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of joined debate — Sāṅkhya fairly stated then page-turned. Downward-facing nature; tatekṣaṇāt settled-equivalent per UNC. Rejected: (a) reopening parse → killed settled. Read aloud: OWN-na-TURE in-DEED … TO-ward THE-bo-dy's ORD-ain-ing.

lines: Own-nature indeed — and this of this — from root-cause-seeing on;
below mind-ground, toward the body's ordaining.
l4.sanskrit_cite: svabhāva eva caiṣo'sya mūlahetostathekṣaṇāt cittabhūmeradharataḥ śarīrādividhiṃ prati
notes: tatekṣaṇāt both parses equivalent in force

reads_against.argmap: What is own-nature for? → Own-nature faces downward: from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining.
c1_essence: Sāṅkhya stated at full strength: pradhāna proved by presence, purposed by denying self-aims; change easy; only striving moves; nature faces down (vv19-22).
The page turns on admitted karma: where is His business? Let His triggering be conceived; seed imaged; Sāṅkhya godless; conditional close (vv23-27).
